subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is checking whether 'summarizing the events' is the same as 'finding out who did it'.
source_quote: Checking it against what we'd actually been told. "True? I thought we were asked to find out what — well, I guess summarizing the events is pretty much the same as finding out who did it from one."

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believes fictional detectives have perfect memories.
source_quote: "I don't know if they do," Thorin said. "I think real detectives just write everything down." "Poirot never does." "No, he doesn't. It's like, at the end of the episode, he's like, okay, everybody sit down, I'm gonna tell you what's what." There was a warmth in it I rarely heard from him. "My wife and I have watched the entire series, and we're down to the last episode, and we're saving it. I'm not sure for why, but —" I let them have it. I was running a different question, the one Thorin eventually asked aloud as we walked. "Who are we working for, exactly?" "Justice," said Grygum. The first rule of any House: know who holds the debt before you decide whether to collect it. Thorin, in his blunt giant-raised way, got to the same place from the other direction. "I guess, who has the power to fire us and tell us to go away?" Bookwyrm. Of course Bookwyrm. We were working for Bookwyrm, and Thorin — who hates the whole rotten apparatus of who-knows-what — put the obvious crack in it before I had to. "I'm just saying, like, if Bookwyrm ended up doing it, which I don't think she did, but… then." A beat. "This could get awkward." It could. I sorted her into the column marked *not above suspicion* and kept walking. The Council of the Great Readers had dispersed. We came into the chapter house to find her already in conference with someone new — a slender half-elf, perhaps fifty, bald scalp framed by black side whiskers chiseled down into a precise goatee. I would have liked to know what they were saying before the door opened. So would everyone. We tried; the trouble is that I had the right tools for reading a page — through a closed door, those tools were the wrong shape entirely. Whatever passed between them, it stayed between them. The moon elf scribes moved to halt us at the threshold. Bookwyrm waved them off and ushered us in herself, all warmth, and introduced the man as Kei Tigersteel — Lorekeeper of Candlekeep, priest of the Temple of Oghma, "the library's spiritual leader." I noted the seating and the easy way she dismissed him a moment later: *yes, Kei, you can take the body to the Shrine of Oghma for purification.* The body went to be purified. Now she was alone with us, which I also noted. "Have you concluded your investigation of the crime scene?" Very serious now. We had. Grygum confirmed it plainly. Thorin pressed her to keep the room sealed, and she agreed three times over — *of course, of course, of course* — which is two more agreements than a thing requires. Then she took us to a nearby room, Deneir's Sanctum, a little shrine and library given over to the art of writing, and offered it up as our office. Fembris would fetch any witness we named. Vooshadi Moonriver would stand the door — *we wouldn't want anyone the investigators don't want to come in, to come in.* And one more thing, lightly placed: we shouldn't move through Candlekeep without one of them. The library is very easy to get lost in. I have an alternative reading of generosity, which is that it is rarely free. "Do we think the room is, like, bugged," I asked the others once we had a moment, "or has, like, secret — like, the stuff we do in there is actually going to be private to us, or do we need —" I kept going, because the offer was too clean. "It's nice and all to offer up that we can use the office, and that they'll go fetch people, and all of those sorts of things, but it's also a little suspect. Like, maybe they're involved, and somehow…" "It doesn't seem just friendly," Grygum said. I asked him to say it again. "It doesn't seem just friendly." "It could be just friendly." I meant it as a hypothesis to be tested, not a comfort. "I mean, it could be that they genuinely want to get to the bottom of this." "Yeah," I said. "It could be." Both columns stayed open. She wanted to know what we'd told her. So did I — it pays to know exactly how much of an account you've already handed over. "Generalities," I said. "That we went and talked to all the people that we could talk to. And we're forming an opinion on what may have happened, and who — like, we have a couple suspects that we would like to pursue, due to perceiving that they may have a motivation, or that other people have pointed them out. We're still —" "Is there any — any suspects in particular?" The question came a half-step too fast. "We refuse to comment on ongoing," Thorin said. "Yeah," I added, "it's an ongoing investigation, and it's not, not proper for us to share that at this time." "Very well," she said. And then she sat there, and she did the thing I'd been waiting for. "Was there nobody that you wished to start your investigation with?" That is not an idle question. That is a question that wants a name back so it can measure where we're pointed. Thorin deflected — *not quite sure who we're gonna talk to next, but you shouldn't read into that* — and I gave her one harmless witness to chew on, Ms. Hollypocket, whom we'd already seen anyway. A name that costs nothing tells you what the asker does with a name. What she did was want Sylvira Savikas. She never said it. She didn't have to; the want came off her like heat off the smelters. Someone had impersonated Sylvira — Grygum thought it made perfect sense, and tactically it did, the impersonated woman might know who would wear her face. It also meant the most powerful person in this building had a strong, unstated preference about where we aimed first. I sorted it: *Bookwyrm steers toward Sylvira.* I had no idea yet whether that was the helpful instinct of someone who wants the thing solved, or a thumb on the scale of an investigation she'd rather not have tilted toward herself. I left that account open too. Then the practical question — together or apart. Thorin liked us as a wall. "It's more imposing to have all, like, you know, four, five, seven, eight, ten of us show up in a room." Grygum wanted to start together and branch later. The reasoning was simple enough: split, and we cover the poison and Sylvira at once, but each of us walks into his own conversation alone, no second pair of hands to steady the work. "Since we're separated, whatever each of us draws, that's what we're stuck with," Thorin said. That was the trade. More ground, less margin. I could live with that. --- ## Thorin — Investigation Strategy and Suspect Review I have spent enough time in the Underdark to know what a bugged room feels like, and Deneir's Sanctum felt like a gift, which is the same thing. Bookwyrm waved us into it like she was doing us a favor. "Well, you can use this room as your office to interview anyone you wish as part of your investigation, and you can rely on Fembris Lancer to catch… fetch any suspects and witnesses you wish to speak to." Catch. She said catch and corrected herself to fetch. I kept that. Daz had the same itch I did. "Do… do we think the room is, like, bugged, or has, like, secret…" He couldn't even finish it. "It's nice and all to offer up that, like, we can use the office, and that they'll go fetch people, and all of those sorts of things, but it's also a little suspect. Like, maybe they're involved, and somehow…" "It doesn't seem just friendly," Grygum said. "I mean, it could be that they genuinely want to get to the bottom of this." That's Grygum. He leaves the door open for people to be decent even while he's bolting it. This is the thing about murder among scholars. Back home — and I mean the mountain, the giants — if you wanted to know who broke a thing, you asked, and someone told you, because lying about it was beneath them. Down here, everybody's got a door they won't open. I hate it. I've always hated it. So when Bookwyrm fished — "Oh, d-do… is there any… Any suspects in particular?" — I gave her the only honest thing I had, which was nothing. "We refuse to comment on ongoing." Daz cleaned it up the way he does. "Yeah, it's an ongoing investigation, and it's not, not proper for us to share that at this time." She tried again. Asked if there was anybody we wished to start with. I shrugged at her. "We're gonna talk to anybody who might be involved, so, you know — not quite sure who we're gonna talk to next, but you shouldn't read into that." What I wanted to read into was her. "I also want to understand where Bookwyrm was before nine in the morning," I said, once we were our own again. "Timeline of where she was. So, available to be a suspect." Everyone's available until they're not. That's not cynicism. That's just keeping the list honest. Grygum was paging through our notes and frowning. "You know, there is somebody in our list of characters who seems to have the same priorities that we do. Maybe that would be someone to interview to sort of get tips on what to do next, or their suspicions." He squinted. "It isn't… for some reason, there's no name on that entry. It just says, Fheminor Scrivenbark." Our own notes had started lying to us. That felt about right for this place. Then the constraint landed — that we'd only get to chase a handful of threads before the thing moved on without us. "Sounds like bullshit," I said, because it was. "I know, but, like, why do we get it, like, what's the hurry? Investigations take as long as they take." Apparently they don't. Apparently things keep happening while you're standing around thinking. Grygum put it plainest: "There'll be more murders." So we wouldn't split, not yet. "I like us sticking together," I said. "I just think it's more imposing to have all, like, you know, five, seven, ten of us show up in a room." Grygum agreed we'd start together and peel off when two doors opened at once. We walked the council back through. The whole pack of them, shouting over a body. A'lai Aivenmore wanting a vote and new leadership. The dowdy halfling, Fheminor Scrivenbark, asking whether Janussi had named a successor. Kazryn Nyantani — slender, gray, those wrinkles around the eyes — cutting through with first you must find the murderer. The bronze dragonborn, Alkrist, formidable and furious, the gate warden needs to be dismissed, this happened on his watch. Bookwyrm trying to settle the room. And Daral not even in it — he'd been at the Hearth, asking why isn't Sylvira Savikas here. Which was the better question. Sylvira wasn't at the council. Sylvira — or somebody wearing her face — had been walking the halls in the dead of night with a lantern. "Someone impersonating her," Zalthir said. "Yes. Yes." Here's where I planted my boots. "I feel like physical evidence is more reliable than trying to parse who's lying and who's not, you know?" Down here everyone lies as a reflex. You can't out-talk a culture that talks for a living. But a smear of poison on a dead man's fingers doesn't have a motive. "But, you know, maybe that's from watching too much CSI, what do I know?" We had a sample of the stuff — off his fingers, and his lip too, Zalthir made sure of that. Grygum volunteered. "I'm happy to do the library research. Poison section, please." And Daz raised the other thread, the one nobody wanted to touch: "There's a missing part of, like, a book that should not be missing… that could have happened a hundred years ago or something, but… seems suspicious, and maybe related." Then we worked the list of people like a vein of ore, deciding where to dig. Daz took Fheminor. "I'm looking at the ones that have the least amount of time, or probably have the least amount to talk about, because sometimes those are the ones that have the most insight." Reasonable. I started down the names. "So, Bookwyrm — do we really think Bookwyrm might have done it? Do we want to give Bookwyrm the third degree?" The warning came back sharp: if we accuse her, we'd better have facts, real ones. "Right," I said, "well, we want to know, we're pretty sure, before we accuse anybody." That's the rule. You don't say the word. Not until you're sure. Daral, we crossed off — not by evidence, by gut. "It's too on the nose for it to be Daral. I don't think it's Daral." Zalthir nodded. "Reading the whole board, I don't think it's Daral." Sylvira, same logic, different reason. "Again, it's someone wore her face, is what we're talking about. I think the whole lantern aspect of it means that it probably wasn't them. She might know something, but it probably wasn't her." Which left the key. "So, I think, Kalan Strongbranch, we gotta interview." Zalthir was already there. "I'm more curious if he still has his other tower key." Two keys to the high towers. Janussi held one. "Yeah, the key is definitely a thread to pull on." Zalthir handed Daz his marching orders for Fheminor — find out when the man got beaten up, because beat-up-at-eight tells a different story than beat-up-when-he-died. Daz: "He wasn't dead yet, but was he beat up?" Zalthir: "He was beat up before he was dead." And whether the man noticed anything missing. And, Zalthir added flat as a tombstone, "if he poisoned the guy when he visited, perchance." One thing kept gnawing me, though, so I backed us up. "Kalan said they'd put the question to the corpse, and that it didn't work. And that didn't work because of Y." The imposter — the false devil-lady — supposedly did it first and locked the corpse's mouth shut for days. Maybe. "Do we know that for sure? I mean, if Kalan's just saying, hey, I did it, but didn't do it? None of us can wring words out of a dead man, so it's not like we can verify, but — whether the corpse was ever truly made to answer is hearsay." I let it sit a beat. "It's also heresy, but…"

subject: Thorin

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin does not argue when Kalan calls the investigators outsiders who were hired to bungle the case.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believes Kalan chose Grygum to receive the key deliberately, not by chance.
source_quote: The key went to Grygum. I marked that before anything else — not into Daz's hand, not into Thorin's, not into the open air for whoever was closest. Kalan stepped out of a doorway we hadn't clocked... He chose the orc. I don't think it was chance.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir tells Kalan they are only there because someone put them up to it and they are happy to not get involved — and believes this to be true.
source_quote: "Purely accidental," I told him. "We have no particular involvement here. Someone put us up to this. We are happy to not get involved." True enough. Filed under things that are also true.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir realizes Kalan was hasty in assuming the murderer was the one who rifled the safe, and corrects him by pointing out the key was in the locket.
source_quote: I stopped him. The key was in the locket. The locket was around the keeper's neck. The locket was gone. So why would the killer go through the safe at all?

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir suspects Kalan is being set up to fail and that the real凶手 is being protected by Bookwyrm or someone else.
source_quote: He suspected, he said, was that one of the Great Readers was the murderer, and that either Bookwyrm was protecting them or someone had convinced her to fire him to protect themselves.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir thinks Kalan is at risk of being killed over a key he no longer has and warns him to watch his back because shapeshifters exist.
source_quote: "Given that you're at risk of being killed over a key you don't have anymore, watch your back," I told him. "Keep in mind there are people who can change their form. Shapeshift. Whatever you want to call it."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believes Kalan is a good investigator who is being deliberately sidelined and that his own team has already outperformed him.
source_quote: "Is he aware that someone was pretending to be Sylvira Savikas the night of the murder?" He went still. "No. That is new information." A pause. "You are very good at this."

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum remembers that midnight tears poison only takes effect at midnight, matching the time of death.
source_quote: The creature that ingests this poison suffers no effect until the stroke of midnight. "That is a good match for, for the... what actually happened," I said. "He died at roughly midnight."

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum realizes the poison was delivered via the book because the victim licked his fingers while reading, causing the poison to react with saliva and darken.
source_quote: Some liquid had gotten onto his finger, and the finger had gone black. Thorin asked the right thing — was the black the poison going dark as it took hold? No. The dust stays pale ochre. What darkens it is saliva. The ochre reacts on contact with spit, and a man turning pages licks his fingers to do it.

source_quote: Oh, I see," I said, "so you can put it someplace, you can throw it into a river or whatever. Nobody will find it, and then when you need it back, boom.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum finds the book *Fey-mous Flowers & Fungi* by Archibald Roots, Jr., and feels it was almost as if the book leaned into his hand.
source_quote: And then I found it faster than I had any right to. The right book practically leaned into my hand — a volume titled *Fey-mous Flowers & Fungi*, by one Archibald Roots, Jr., son of the legendary gnome botanist Archibald Roots Sr. I almost laughed.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum feels a sense of peace and focus in the library, contrasting with his past underground experiences.
source_quote: It is a strange thing, after months underground, to research in a room with shelves taller than the ceilings I'd learned to stoop beneath. No Faerzress humming behind my eyes. No tunnel that might put an enemy in front of me by the time I turned a page. Just stacks, and quiet, and the work.

We were to go to the Hearth. I noted the inversion before we'd even left the room — the suspect setting the venue, picking the ground, making the famous detectives walk to him.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral believes he was drugged and upset when the incident with Janussi occurred.
source_quote: I was drugged. I was upset. I don't know what I was thinking.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir wishes the Whispering Dome were quiet and undisturbed, as he has spent his life seeking such spaces.
source_quote: The Whispering Dome was the kind of place I would have liked under different circumstances. Quiet. Low light pooling under the curve of the ceiling. No one talking unless they had a reason. I have spent most of my life looking for rooms like this, and most of my life finding them already occupied by people who would not stop making noise.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir recalls attending a class on silent communication but cannot remember the lesson.
source_quote: I remember the light through the shutters. I do not remember the lesson.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir realizes Glabbagool mastered the lesson of stillness that he himself failed to learn.
source_quote: The student on my arm had mastered the one lesson I most thoroughly missed, and he had done it in under a minute, by going still.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir feels excitement about Glabbagool’s abilities and his new form.
source_quote: This is exciting. We formed Voltron or something.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir prefers that Glabbagool blend into his scales rather than appear as a separate creature with obvious eyes.
source_quote: I suggested he might not need them — that he could blend into me rather than read as a separate creature riding along.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir acknowledges he has slept through many important lessons.
source_quote: There are, by now, a great many days I was sleeping.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir intends to keep checking on the drow in the bag of holding, as Glabbagool reminded him.
source_quote: Well, either way, as long as you check in on the drow, we're all good.

subject: Glabbagool's transformation
fact: Glabbagool and Zalthir are now permanently bound, with Glabbagool settling on Zalthir’s arm and integrating with his physiology.
source_quote: Glabbagool and Zalthir, together now, he said, settling along my forearm like he had measured it in advance.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool remembers waiting a long time to bond with Zalthir.
source_quote: I've been waiting to do this for a very long time.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool believes he must be quiet, and he values that requirement.
source_quote: Then he added that it must be quiet, and I liked that more.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool thinks people expect him to have large, obvious eyes and considers blending them into Zalthir’s scales.
source_quote: He thought people expected him to have them, large and obvious.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool’s instinct, even at the moment of transformation, is to ensure housekeeping tasks like monitoring the drow are completed.
source_quote: his instinct, at the moment of his own transformation, was housekeeping.
